channel.title: Does browser-choice include additional AppArmor profiles?
channel.description: @arraybolt3 does browser choice ship any separate apparmor that are not already included with kicksecure? Might be a good idea to look at and readjust, or add any that aren't shipped for these browsers in browser choice. I noticed sum things when looking at AA rules, but I'll post them elsewhere.

item.title: Does browser-choice include additional AppArmor profiles?
item.dc:creator: init38
item.description:
arraybolt3:

Note that apparmor.d is not a Kicksecure project, that’s a fork of it we have for some development investigation. It doesn’t ship as part of Kicksecure yet, although it could at some (undefined but likely distant) point in the future.

Ohh ok thanks I was under the impression it was bundled in but thanks for clarifying that up.

arraybolt3:

Be aware that AppArmor in Debian Trixie does not have working UNIX socket or D-Bus mediation, therefore any process that has any access to UNIX sockets has full access to D-Bus. This will hopefully be fixed in Debian Forky with AppArmor 5.

I’ll have to try to track that progress on Forky and mailing lists. Thanks for the heads up on that.

item.dc:creator: init38
item.description:
Brave does not ship a apparmor profile by default.

github.com/brave/brave-browser

AppArmor problem when running Brave on Ubuntu 24.04 (installed via apt)

opened 12:31AM - 14 Sep 24 UTC
andyrozman
OS/Linux OS/Desktop

### Description Brave doesn't have apparmor profile. Since 24.04 it seems appar…mor needs to be running... I tried with profiles from several sources, I even tried to train my own profile, but Brave (and all other chromium based browsers) fail to start. 2024-09-14T00:01:50.817601+01:00 SeaQuest kernel: audit: type=1400 audit(1726268510.816:88): apparmor="DENIED" operation="userns_create" class="namespace" info="Userns create restricted - failed to find unprivileged_userns profile" error=-13 profile="unconfined" pid=6151 comm="brave" requested="userns_create" denied="userns_create" target="unprivileged_userns" ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install brave (via apt install brave-browser) on newly installed Ubuntu 24.04.1 2. Run brave ### Actual result Application doesn't start. In /var/log/kern.log you will find something like this: 2024-09-14T00:01:50.817601+01:00 SeaQuest kernel: audit: type=1400 audit(1726268510.816:88): apparmor="DENIED" operation="userns_create" class="namespace" info="Userns create restricted - failed to find unprivileged_userns profile" error=-13 profile="unconfined" pid=6151 comm="brave" requested="userns_create" denied="userns_create" target="unprivileged_userns" ### Expected result Browser starts ### Reproduces how often Easily reproduced ### Brave version (brave://version info) Brave: 1.69.168 OS: Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS ### Channel information - [X] release (stable) - [ ] beta - [ ] nightly ### Reproducibility - [ ] with Brave Shields disabled - [ ] with Brave Rewards disabled - [ ] in the latest version of Chrome ### Miscellaneous information Like I said I tried different profiles from different sources and while some worked better, none of them allowed me to start application. Only solution was workaround, problem is that I have to do every time I start the machine. sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=0 sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0

One does ship one via apparmor.d brave profile and might I say it looks pretty locked down while not being too restrictive.

Had to put my readers on cuz I almost read that it granted access to calling abstractions/bus/ like network-manager-observe. Which means it could possibly call a interfaces HwAddress via D-Bus but it looks like it doesn’t have D-Bus access to NetworkManager

item.title: Does browser-choice include additional AppArmor profiles?
item.dc:creator: arraybolt3
item.description:
desi_fubu:

does browser choice ship any separate apparmor that are not already included with kicksecure?

For a very technical answer that’s what you asked for but not what you wanted to ask for, no. browser-choice is already included with Kicksecure, so any AppArmor profiles it ships now or in the future are included with Kicksecure.

For an answer closer to what you wanted but probably still not quite there, also no. browser-choice itself includes zero AppArmor profiles (as you can verify by visiting GitHub - Kicksecure/browser-choice: Browser choice for Kicksecure - lets the user pick the default browser at first run · GitHub and searching for “apparmor” in the “Go to file” box). No part of browser-choice itself needs confined by AppArmor, so there is no need for additional profiles.

I think what you meant to ask is, does browser-choice provide AppArmor profiles that confine individual web browsers beyond the level of confinement they would have by default? To answer that, no, browser-choice doesn’t ship any configuration, AppArmor profiles or otherwise, that alter the behavior of a browser. It is only an installer, and will very likely remain that way by design. Developing special configuration for a web browser is essentially in-house browser development, which we explicitly avoid:

Kicksecure – 19 May 26

In-House Browser Development - Kicksecure Default Browser - Development...

Not possible with the current available project resources. See also Too Much Source Code, Too Much Complexity and Difficulty to Create a Browser. | Exploring the ideal default browser for Kicksecure with a focus on security and privacy, browser...

(We do a little bit of pre-configuration for Tor Browser, but that’s an exception to the rule since Tor Browser is essential to Whonix, and we need special configuration for Tor Browser for it to work with Whonix.)
